title: <SUP>12</SUP>CO emission from the Red Rectangle
question: What are the morphology, temperature, density and kinematics of the CO gas envelope of the Red Rectangle, from archival ALMA CO(3-2) and CO(6-5) data?

what.value: Dust temperature and CO density model for comparison

evidence.quote: the dust temperature quoted by Men’shchikov et al. (2002) decreases from $\sim$80 K at $r$=1$''$ to $\sim$60 K at $r$=2.5$''$

recipe.method: Rearrange cubes to 50x50 pixels, 5''x5'', 36 velocity bins of 0.40 km/s, rotated 13 deg, centred on continuum; keep pixels above flux thresholds (1526 pixels)
Iteratively solve F(y,z)=∫ρ(ξ,z)dx assuming rotational symmetry, 35 ξ bins x 50 z bins of 0.1''
key_parameters: uncertainties: absolute 0.16 (3-2) and 2.2 (6-5) Jy arcsec^-2 plus 20% relative; ten iterations

recipe.method: Joint chi2 fit of equatorial rotation+expansion and parabolic polar outflow model to velocity spectra of both lines

evidence.quote: their ratio, 4.3, corresponds to an average temperature of 63 K
the star axis is inclined by $\sim$8$^\circ$ from the North away the Earth
The integrated fluxes are 0.66$\pm$0.10 Jy at 345 GHz and 4.0$\pm$0.6 Jy at 690 GHz
